regions.name: Asia
regions.text: Building sites and estates: models from the architect's drawings, checked on site with phone scans and a drone, and twins that sell homes before they are built.

regions.name: Europe
regions.text: Existing buildings measured and handed over as Revit-ready IFC with plans, sections and elevations, so the specialists start from a model instead of a site visit.

regions.name: Middle East
regions.text: Paper permits and old drawings turned into real models, so buildings can be divided, sold and let on their true areas.

regions.name: Africa
regions.text: Capture that works like Matterport without the camera: inspectors scan with the phones they already have, the data lands in the company's own account, and the drawings follow.

regions.name: Oceania
regions.text: Design studios scan, model and publish their own projects with the free iOS app and BIM Author.

regions.name: Americas
regions.text: Canada and Latin America are still to start, with earlier scan-to-model work on record. The United States is not offered.

markets.name: Thailand
markets.what: Construction work in Asia, running every day. Villas under construction are modelled from the architect's drawings and checked on site with phone scans and a drone. A development of about 100 homes sells off-plan from its twins, and a restaurant, a padel club and a sports centre run on the same platform.
markets.next: A custom ventilation product with an installer, and sales and rental tools for the whole estate.

markets.name: Sweden
markets.what: Advanced BIM for a developed market. Existing buildings handed over as Revit-ready IFC with drawings, for the energy, ventilation and structural specialists who already work in Revit and ArchiCAD. A demo villa on Swedish coordinates shows the sun study in Nordic light.
markets.next: A guest lecture and demo for technical property managers, and a Swedish partner.

markets.name: Lebanon
markets.label: Middle East
markets.what: Digitizing the Middle East. A 14-storey tower over four basements, modelled from 300 dpi scans of paper permits. The owners had a price per square metre but not the real size of each flat; the model gives every flat its true area.
markets.next: Floor plans for sale and rental, and the next towers.

markets.name: Australia
markets.what: Designers working on their own scans. An interior design studio has used Skanna on its own projects since August: scanned with the free iOS app, modelled in BIM Author, published as twins. Its review: the templates solve about 90% of the setup.
markets.next: A full house with pool and garden, six scans stitched in the browser. Sell to teams with CAD staff first.

markets.name: South Africa
markets.what: Matterport-like capture for Africa. Most properties have no approved plans for what stands, and deals stall at transfer. Inspectors scan with their phones, the data lands in the firm's own account, and the compliance drawings follow.
markets.next: A scan-and-model firm covering South Africa and Namibia is testing the platform.

markets.name: Spain
markets.what: The next market, through real estate. Independent agencies win the listing with a twin and a real floor plan, captured with a phone, for buyers who cannot fly in. Developers on the coast sell off-plan the way Falcon Hill does.
markets.next: Introductions to agencies south of Madrid and in Almería, through a go-to-market adviser on success fee.

markets.name: Estonia
markets.what: Skanna OÜ is registered in Tallinn. Estonia is the company's EU base, so GDPR is the floor for every market.

markets.name: United States
markets.what: Not offered. No sign-ups, sales or marketing in the United States. Earlier work here, 2021 to 2025, is shown by year and project type only.

markets.name: Canada
markets.what: Earlier scan-to-model work for clients here, 2021 to 2025. Nothing running now.
